consensus_summary: No single settled symbolic meaning for 'day'; it is highly context-dependent. Common/primary uses across responses include day as the realm of light, righteousness, moral wakefulness and opportunity (vs. night/darkness); the Day of the Lord as eschatological judgment/salvation; extended periods/ages; the day-year principle (minority/historicist); and day as a thousand years. Literal 24-hour use is also frequent.
book_summary: Day as the time of light for exposure and accountability (deeds seen and tested), the season to walk, work and watch; the children of light are the children of the day; and, in the prophets’ counts, a scalable unit (day for a year in judgment; one day with the Lord as a thousand years).
consensus_core_identification: Day as light/righteousness/spiritual alertness (or, alternatively, the appointed eschatological Day of the Lord), with separate recognized alternatives for time-scaling.
book_core_identification: Day as the time of light involving exposure, accountability and the season for work/watchfulness (children of day = children of light), simultaneously a scalable prophetic/divine time unit.
boundary_disagreement: The book unifies the light/moral-wakefulness motif with the day-year and day=1000-year scalings into a single core entry, whereas consensus keeps the scalings as distinct alternatives or minority readings separate from the light symbolism; it also adds the precision of 'exposure and accountability when deeds are seen and tested'.
material_contradiction: None; the book selects and combines uses that appear as primary or alternative meanings across the consensus responses without denying any of them.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap heavily: the book's 'time of light... children of the day' is equivalent to the primary light/righteousness identification in B/C/D (and a common alternative in A), while its scaling clauses match alternatives listed in every response. Extra wording ('exposure and accountability', 'season to walk, work and watch') and the composite presentation refine boundaries and extension rather than replace the referent, yielding REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT. No consensus core is contradicted.
strongest_objection: Day-year (and fixed day=1000) readings are tradition-specific/minority rather than pan-Christian, so integrating them as definitional may over-unify context-dependent usages that consensus keeps separate.
